widget.name: Vega Chart
widget.description: Renders a Vega-Lite or Vega specification. The spec is authored once and held here; only the data comes from the model.

property.caption: Specification
property.description: Vega-Lite or Vega JSON. Which language is used is decided by the spec's own $schema, so both are accepted here. Any "data" in the spec is replaced by the Data property below when that is set.

property.caption: Data
property.description: A JSON array of row objects, bound to the spec's named dataset (or to its top-level data when no name is given). Kept separate from the spec so the model never has to generate layout.

property.caption: Dataset name
property.description: The name the spec uses to refer to the data (Vega-Lite: {"data": {"name": "table"}}). Leave empty to replace the spec's top-level data instead.

property.caption: Selection
property.description: Written with the clicked mark's datum as JSON. Only the datum's own scalar fields are included — Vega's internal bookkeeping is stripped, so what arrives is the row the model emitted.

property.caption: On click
property.description: Runs after the selection attribute is written. Leave empty to make the chart read-only; clicks are then ignored entirely rather than being written and discarded.

property.caption: Height (px)
property.description: Height of the chart container. Zero lets the container take the height the chart renders at, which is what a chart sized by its data needs — a facet row per category or a legend entry per series has no height the page can know in advance.

property.caption: Renderer
property.description: SVG keeps marks selectable and styleable by CSS; canvas is faster for very dense charts.

property.caption: Show actions menu
property.description: Vega's own export / view-source menu. Off by default so the chart carries no chrome of its own.
